## EXECUTED: gate-scratch volume is in service on i-00880b2c7f13527c5

Ran `infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md` §§2-10 end to end on 2026-09-06 (UTC), via AWS SSM
`send-command` (no SSH on this host). All acceptance conditions met and confirmed from CloudWatch.
**Not closing** — leaving that to the operator.

### §0 pre-change state (PROVEN, read-only, 01:42 UTC)

```
NAME          SERIAL               FSTYPE SIZE MOUNTPOINT
nvme0n1       vol0270fcf13709cf472         60G
├─nvme0n1p1                        xfs     60G /
└─nvme0n1p128                      vfat    10M /boot/efi
nvme1n1       vol06fa2e77a9dd97527 xfs     50G /var/gerrit
nvme2n1       vol06780b8557d1416b7         50G            <-- target: no FSTYPE, no MOUNTPOINT

/dev/nvme0n1p1   60G   42G   19G  70% /
blkid /dev/nvme2n1  -> NO FILESYSTEM
grep gate-scratch /etc/fstab -> no fstab line
mountpoint /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch -> is not a mountpoint
.gate-scratch-required / .gate-scratch-mounted -> both No such file or directory
```

Matches the runbook's expected table on every row except `df /`, which read **70% (42G)** rather
than the documented **81% (49G)**. Benign drift: `root_disk_used_percent` shows 82% at 18:12 PDT
falling to 69% by 18:22, i.e. the disk-pressure pruner reclaimed ~12% between the runbook being
written and this execution.

### Authorisation for the irreversible `mkfs.xfs` (PROVEN)

Device resolved **by serial, never by name**, immediately before the format, with two interlocks:

```
  candidate /dev/nvme0n1 serial=[vol0270fcf13709cf472]
  candidate /dev/nvme1n1 serial=[vol06fa2e77a9dd97527]
  candidate /dev/nvme2n1 serial=[vol06780b8557d1416b7]
resolved DEV=[/dev/nvme2n1] matches=1
root=/dev/nvme0n1p1 gerrit=/dev/nvme1n1 target=/dev/nvme2n1
interlock: target unmounted OK
interlock: blkid reports NO FILESYSTEM on /dev/nvme2n1 -- format authorised
```

The runbook's warning about NVMe enumeration is not theoretical and reproduced here: **after the
reboot below, `lsblk` listed `nvme1n1` FIRST**, ahead of `nvme0n1`. Ordering moved within this very
session; only the serial join was stable.

### §3-§6 (PROVEN)

```
mkfs.xfs /dev/nvme2n1 -> mkfs_rc=0
/dev/nvme2n1: UUID="7ea719fd-f65c-4e8f-992c-d74410b5ea4c" BLOCK_SIZE="512" TYPE="xfs"

UUID=7ea719fd-f65c-4e8f-992c-d74410b5ea4c /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch xfs defaults,nofail 0 2
mount_a_rc=0
MOUNTED
/dev/nvme2n1     50G  390M   50G   1% /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch
grep -c gate-scratch /etc/fstab -> 1
findmnt --verify -> Success, no errors or warnings detected
```

Markers written **proof-first**, per §6, and verified as the *property* rather than the filenames:

```
/var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required             10303   (ROOT)
/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/.gate-scratch-mounted 10302   (VOLUME)
PASS: markers on DIFFERENT filesystems (10303 vs 10302)
drwx------. root root /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch
```

Ordering rationale, restated because it is load-bearing: the DECLARATION on root is what makes gate
admission refuse when the proof is missing. Writing it first would open a window in which every gate
on the box refuses; writing the PROOF first has no bad window, because proof-without-declaration is
exactly the (silent) state the host was already in. `chmod 0700` precedes both so no marker is ever
written into a world-readable directory.

### §7 review-bot recreate — the split-brain check (PROVEN)

`docker compose up -d --force-recreate review-bot`, then **from inside the container**:

```
/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch 10302
/var/lib/rebar               10303        <-- DIFFER: container sees the VOLUME
ls -a /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch -> .gate-scratch-mounted
/dev/nvme2n1     50G  390M   50G   1% /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch
/dev/nvme0n1p1   60G   42G   19G  70% /var/lib/rebar
write test: /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/.writetest 10302  WRITE_OK
```

Confirmed `docker-compose.yml:305` binds `/var/lib/rebar` (the PARENT) — so §7's mandatory recreate
is correct as written. `compose-review-bot-1` reached `healthy`, `/health` -> `{"status":"ok"}`,
and served a review (`in_flight:1`) shortly after.

### §8 reclaim (PROVEN)

```
before: /dev/nvme0n1p1  60G  42G  19G  70% /     (43958564 KB used)
RM_DONE rc=0 at Sun Sep  6 02:59:38 UTC 2026
after:  /dev/nvme0n1p1  60G  19G  42G  32% /     (19800344 KB used)
```

**~23 GiB reclaimed from root; 70% -> 32%.** Ran detached on the host (finite tree, polled to
completion) rather than in-line, so it could not block the SSM worker.

### §9 CloudWatch — confirmed with DATAPOINTS, not StateReason (PROVEN)

```
gate_scratch_mounted            19:45 1.0   19:50 1.0   19:55 1.0     (was 0.0 for days)
disk_used_percent  mount=/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch
                                19:45 1.0   19:50 6.0   19:55 5.0     (was NO DATAPOINTS)
root_disk_used_percent          19:45 70.0  19:50 56.0  19:55 45.0

rebar-gate-scratch-disk-high   OK   since 2026-09-05T19:46:44 PDT
rebar-gate-scratch-unmounted   OK   since 2026-09-05T19:46:55 PDT
```

The caveat about the observability probe truncating did **not** apply: `disk_used_percent` resumed
publishing normally, and `probe_ok=1` / `probe_truncated=0` throughout. No ambiguity to report.
Live gate traffic is now landing on the volume — `rebar-gate-snapshots` and `semgrep-mcp` have been
recreated there and it is at 2.1G/5%.

### §10 detector (PROVEN)

```
$ terraform show -json > tf.json
$ python scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py --plan-json tf.json --instance-id i-00880b2c7f13527c5
in-service      vol-06780b8557d1416b7  /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch  -- mounted
in-service      vol-06fa2e77a9dd97527  /var/gerrit  -- mounted
exit=0
```

(Before this procedure it would have named `vol06780b8557d1416b7` NOT-IN-SERVICE and exited 1.)

---

## INCIDENT DURING EXECUTION — I wedged the host, and it is my error

**What happened.** Reaching for §2's quiescence evidence, I ran
`lsof +D /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`. That recursively walks the tree and builds an in-memory
table; the directory held 226 snapshot directories. Memory went
`43% -> 33% -> 23% -> 21% -> 4%` available (`mem_used_percent` 95%), the SSM agent stopped pinging
at 19:09:18 PDT, and every `rebar/host` metric ended at 19:08. SSM went `ConnectionLost`; run-command
invocations sat `Pending` indefinitely. It did not self-recover in ~30 minutes.

**This was avoidable and the runbook told me so.** §1 states a read-only `du -sh` over this same
directory had not finished after 25 minutes and that "this runbook therefore never depends on `du`".
`lsof +D` is the same class of operation — worse, because it also allocates. I ran it anyway.

**Recovery.** Diagnosed against `infra/runbooks/gerrit-host-wedged-ssm-lost.md`. Distinguished this
from that runbook's disk-full case: root was at 70% with 19G free and EC2 status checks were `ok`,
so the cause was memory, not disk, and growing the volume was not indicated. Took protective
snapshots (`snap-01e10c794b7abcf0e` gerrit data, `snap-0bae90f11fb67532b` root), then
`aws ec2 reboot-instances`. SSM returned `Online` 4m20s later; Gerrit HTTP 200; all containers up.
The procedure then continued from a re-verified §0 (all preconditions still held).

**Cost:** roughly 35 minutes of host downtime (02:09-02:44 UTC), which took Gerrit with it.
Nothing was lost — no destructive step had run at that point; the `mv`/`mkfs` came afterwards.

**Note on the Gerrit restart:** the standing instruction was not to restart Gerrit unless a runbook
required it. By the time of the reboot Gerrit was *already* down as part of the wedge, and
`gerrit-host-wedged-ssm-lost.md` prescribes a reboot for exactly this signature, so the reboot
restored service rather than interrupting it.

---

## RUNBOOK DRIFT FOUND (each is a real defect, filed here rather than worked around)

**D1 — §2 names the wrong compose directory.** The runbook says
`cd /var/gerrit/compose 2>/dev/null || cd "$(dirname "$(find / -name docker-compose.yml ...)")"`.
`/var/gerrit/compose` **does not exist**; `/var/gerrit` contains only `site/`. The real project dir
is **`/opt/rebar/infra/compose`** (from
`docker inspect compose-review-bot-1 --format '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}'`).
The `find /` fallback would also have walked the whole filesystem on an IOPS-starved box. This is the
same class as the `nginx-edge-render.md` defect (`git fetch` in `/opt/rebar`, which is an rsync copy
with no `.git`).

**D2 — §2's `fuser -vm` quiescence check cannot work, by construction.** `-m` takes a *mountpoint*.
Before the fix `/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` is a plain directory on root, so `fuser -vm` resolves to
`/` and lists **every process on the box** including `systemd`, `kthreadd` and every kernel thread.
The documented expectation "no processes listed" is therefore unreachable in the pre-fix state the
step is written for. Chasing a usable substitute is what led me to `lsof +D` and the outage.
Suggested replacement — bounded, no tree walk, no allocation:

```sh
for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do case "$(readlink $p/cwd 2>/dev/null)" in *gate-scratch*) echo "$p";; esac; done
for f in /proc/[0-9]*/fd/*;  do case "$(readlink $f 2>/dev/null)"     in *gate-scratch*) echo "$f";; esac; done
```

Both returned 0 holders here, in about a second, and combined with a stopped review-bot and an
unchanged top-level mtime that is strictly better evidence than the `fuser` line asks for.

**D3 — no step warns against walking the tree, where it matters most.** §1's "never depends on `du`"
warning is a parenthetical about *duration*. It should be a prohibition attached to §2: do not `du`,
`lsof +D`, `find`, or otherwise recurse `/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` — it will exhaust memory and
wedge the host. Demonstrated tonight.

**D4 — §2 does not mention `rebar-autodeploy.timer`, which fires every 2 minutes.** A
`docker compose stop review-bot` is exposed to a deploy tick landing mid-procedure. I stopped the
timer for the window as a precaution. Reading `autodeploy.sh` afterwards shows the review-bot
rebuild/restart is gated on a source change and the host was already at target SHA
(`12a10f3ab4ef`), so it would have been a no-op — the risk is real but narrow, and it is only
narrow *because* `main` happened not to advance. Worth one sentence in §2. (The timer is `enabled`,
so the reboot restored it automatically; verified `active` afterwards.)

**D5 — §7 recreates only review-bot; confirmed sufficient, worth stating.** I checked every
container for a `/var/lib/rebar` bind, since any other one would have the identical `rprivate`
split-brain problem. Only `compose-review-bot-1` binds it. §7 is complete as written — but the
check is cheap and the reasoning belongs in the runbook:
`docker inspect <c> --format '{{range .Mounts}}{{if eq .Destination "/var/lib/rebar"}}...'`.

---

## PROVEN vs INFERRED

**Proven:** every transcript above — format, UUID fstab line, mount, both markers on distinct
devices, in-container mount visibility and write test, 23 GiB reclaim, CloudWatch datapoints, both
alarms OK, detector exit 0.

**Inferred (not tested):** that the mount survives reboot. The fstab line is by UUID with `nofail`
and `findmnt --verify` passes, which is the mechanism — but I did not reboot again to demonstrate
it, having already spent one unplanned reboot tonight. Cheap to confirm at the next planned restart.

Residual items §11 lists (gate admission still treating "no declaration" as "no volume"; the
expected mount set written per-volume in three places) are untouched and still open.
